approval_note: Owner said 'Yes, add it. Then go' in chat on 2026-08-03, after approving 'ALL of the above' and then sharpening the design across four exchanges. The go bundles: (1) an engine crash on /trips/preview stays HTTP 200 but renders as a LOUD RED failure distinct from a calm policy note; (2) ZERO differences between the two surfaces, NO allowlist, no exceptions -- owner verbatim 'ANY DIFFERENCE. NO EXCEPTIONS. STOP FLINCHING.'; (3) ALL tour code literally SHARED, enforced by a SELF-COMPLETING reachability check, because comparison only detects drift while one implementation prevents it -- owner verbatim 'ALL OF THAT CODE HAS TO BE SHARED. NO DIVERGENCES.'; (4) route sanity FIRST AND FOREMOST, straight-line fallback deleted, unroutable means refused; (5) the winner between the two planning algorithms decided by EXPERIMENT not by incumbency, after the fact-checks are equalised; (6) a periodic model-driven architecture audit added as a WORKLIST-ONLY layer outside the bar. Travel-mode (metro/commute) support is explicitly deferred as a separate feature.

baseline.commit: 68c4f723 on main; working tree clean except untracked scripts/tour_api_preview.py
baseline.note: Containers at plan time: dev Neo4j 7687 UP, Valhalla 8002 UP, test 7688 DOWN, workbench 7689 DOWN. The crash below was reproduced LIVE through `make workbench` with real Render credentials and a real provider on 2026-08-03, not inferred from code reading.

decisions.D1-root-cause: src/tour/degradations.py:86-107 `in_current_context(fn)` captures ONE contextvars.Context at wrap time (:102) and returns a closure calling ctx.run(fn,...) (:105). Both fan-outs wrap ONCE and hand the single closure to a thread pool -- src/tour/premium_tour.py:443 `pool.map(in_current_context(invoke), plan.units)` and src/tour/authoring.py:966 `pool.map(in_current_context(executor.execute), plan.units)`. A Context cannot be entered by two threads at once, so every tour with 2+ stops raises `RuntimeError: cannot enter context: ... is already entered`. Production units are slow provider calls, so the overlap is guaranteed, not probabilistic.
decisions.D2-introduced-by: Commit 4a0ea1f5, 2026-07-31 16:25 -0700, 'feat(api): delete every rate limiter and the paid-call guard; make failures visible' -- the commit that ADDED degradations.py and wired both fan-out sites in the same change. There is no regression window to bisect: it has been 100% broken since that minute. `make audit` was green on it.
decisions.D3-why-the-bar-stayed-green: Three independent blindfolds. (1) src/api/routes/trips.py `except Exception:` returns HTTP 200 with _basic_tour_fallback(reason='llm_generation_failed'). (2) The hermetic suite injects OfflinePremiumExecutor (tests/conftest.py:146-151) whose units complete instantly, so pool workers never overlap. (3) The Playwright shard runs with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY blanked and tests/test_workbench_ui.py::test_workbench_generates_a_real_tour_unstubbed deliberately accepts EITHER lane, so a premium failure is an expected pass there. Net: no test in `make test` exercises premium authoring end to end.
decisions.D4-fix-shape: Keep the wrap-time copy_context() snapshot -- that is what carries the caller's _ACTIVE collector into the worker -- but make _run enter a FRESH context per call via snapshot.copy().run(fn, ...). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION at plan time on this interpreter: contextvars.Context.copy exists; old shape raises the production RuntimeError with 3 slow workers; new shape collects [0,1,2,3] and survives nested fan-outs. REJECTED: contextvars.copy_context() inside _run -- it copies the WORKER's empty context, silently dropping propagation and re-creating the exact invisible-failure bug the module exists to prevent. REJECTED: re-wrapping per call at the two call sites -- fixes two sites and leaves the trap armed for the third.
decisions.D5-fake-guard-test: tests/test_degradations.py::test_a_degradation_recorded_in_a_worker_thread_is_not_lost uses the SAME broken pattern as production (pool.map(in_current_context(_work), range(3))) but _work is an instant no-op, so the three threads never overlap inside the Context. MEASURED: `make test-file FILE=tests/test_degradations.py` -> 6 passed in 0.02s while production crashes 100% of the time. The replacement must force overlap by construction (an Event handshake, NOT a Barrier -- under the bug a Barrier deadlocks because worker 0 blocks inside the entered context forever).
decisions.D6-preview-stays-200: An engine crash on POST /trips/preview keeps HTTP 200 with the Basic stops, and becomes unmissable in the BODY and on SCREEN instead. Rationale: the loudness problem is not the status code, it is that the body says nothing true -- the response already carries candidate_rejection.code/detail and grep shows ZERO consumers in frontend/ or mobile/lib. Verified: the phone never calls /trips/preview (mobile/lib/services/trip_service.dart:61 uses /trips/generate and /trips/{id}/compose), so this endpoint is workbench-only plus the public POC page. This honours prior decision D2 of specs/2026-07-29-one-true-tour-algorithm rather than overriding it. OWNER MAY OVERRIDE -- see run-context.md decision 1.
decisions.D0-one-engine-confirmed: The one-true-tour-algorithm unification IS in force, and it is why a single defect took out every surface at once. TRACED 2026-08-03: the phone's POST /trips/{id}/compose goes trips.py:614 plan_prebuilt_route_authoring -> :630 author_prebuilt_route -> authoring.py:966 pool.map(...) -> the shared finalizer finalize_certification_composition; the workbench's POST /trips/preview goes trips.py:943 plan_premium_tour -> :1013 execute_premium_plan -> premium_tour.py:443 pool.map(...) -> :1018 finalize_premium_tour -> :497 finalize_certification_composition. SAME finalizer, same per-stop prompt, same dedup, same gates. What differs is only the ON-RAMP (compose authors a route already persisted in Neo4j; preview authors one just planned in memory) and the ERROR HANDLING wrapped around it. BOTH on-ramps call the same broken in_current_context helper, which is why both surfaces broke together.
decisions.D7-phone-500-stays: The SAME bug reaches the phone through the other on-ramp (see D0): src/api/routes/trips.py:630 author_prebuilt_route is caught only by ComposeVerificationError and ValueError, and _upstream_provider_errors (:120-129) maps only provider throttle/error/timeout. A RuntimeError is none of these, so a tourist pressing compose today gets a bare HTTP 500. For this slice the 500 STAYS -- it is loud and truthful, i.e. not a silent failure -- with one hard rule added: a crash must NEVER be relabelled compose_verification_failed, because that code means 'the narrator wrote something untraceable' and would blame the writer for an engine fault. Converting it to a graceful 422 needs its own ledger and a mobile change (D1 of the prior ledger pins that wire contract; the phone parses detail['attempts']).
decisions.D8-duplicates-are-a-symptom: The tester's 'duplicate stories' ARE REAL and were reproduced live, but they are in the BASIC FALLBACK text, which performs no de-duplication at all -- not in the premium narration. Measured in the live response: at Square du Vert-Galant Henri IV's nickname is explained FOUR times; at La Samaritaine the naming story is told twice and the founding year is given as both 1870 and 1867 in the same stop. Once premium works the tester never sees Basic prose. Basic-lane de-duplication and the older, still-open PREMIUM semantic-repetition problem are both OUT of this slice.
decisions.D9-no-new-make-targets: Owner ruling in chat: 'You don't need new make targets. You don't need code. You just need to invoke what's already there.' No step adds a Makefile target or new tooling. The one Makefile line change that WOULD be needed (adding a paid live premium test to LIVE_TEST_FILES) is deliberately held out as owner decision 2 in run-context.md, because it alone would raise this ledger to Tier 3.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a callable wrapped once by in_current_context and handed to a pool where worker 0 is provably held INSIDE the wrapper by an Event while worker 1 enters, when they run, then neither raises and BOTH workers' degradations reach the caller's collector. REQUIRED MUTATION: restore the single wrap-time context (snapshot.run instead of snapshot.copy().run) and this goes RED with 'cannot enter context'; separately, move the copy inside _run as contextvars.copy_context().run and the propagation assertion goes RED.

Given a plan of 3+ units and an executor whose workers are forced to overlap, when execute_premium_plan (src/tour/premium_tour.py) and author_prebuilt_route (src/tour/authoring.py) each run, then each returns one response per unit and raises no RuntimeError.

Given a single-unit plan, when it is authored, then it still succeeds and the collected degradation list is EMPTY -- single-stop tours never overlapped and worked throughout the outage; they must keep working and must not start crying wolf.

Given a unit that fails INSIDE either fan-out, when the tour is built, then a degradation carrying the exception type, message and stop index reaches the caller's scope AND the exception is re-raised (a partial premium tour must abort, never ship half-narrated).

Given an executor that raises RuntimeError('MARKER-9f3c'), when POST /trips/preview is called, then the response body contains BOTH 'RuntimeError' and 'MARKER-9f3c'. REQUIRED MUTATION: restore the constant detail string 'Premium authoring did not produce a complete traced blueprint' as the only detail and this goes RED. This is the single criterion that would have caught the outage on day one.

Given the same injection, when the response is read, then degradations has at least one row whose error_type is RuntimeError and whose error_message contains the marker. Separate from AC-5 because an empty degradations list is documented as meaning 'nothing degraded -- a real statement rather than an absence', and today a total crash produces [], so the mechanism actively asserts all-clear during a total failure.

Given an engine crash and given a legitimately non-qualifying tour, when both are requested, then the two responses differ in a machine-readable field a renderer can branch on, and the crash response is not byte-identical to the policy response.

Given an executor that succeeds on every unit, when POST /trips/preview is called, then candidate_eligible is true, basic_tour is null and degradations is []. A warning that is always on is the same as no warning.

Given a parametrised injection of every fault the authoring seam can produce (RuntimeError, ValueError, KeyError, MemoryError, ComposeVerificationError, anthropic.APIError, anthropic.RateLimitError, TimeoutError), when each is injected, then NOT (status==200 AND candidate_eligible AND stops) AND the response names the cause on an observable channel. The test must assert it found its subjects before asserting anything about them.

Given the syntax tree of src/api/routes/trips.py, src/tour/premium_tour.py and src/tour/authoring.py, when every broad `except Exception` on the tour path is walked, then each either re-raises or records a degradation. Derived with ast, never text matching. REQUIRED MUTATION: add a new bare `except Exception: pass` on the tour path and this goes RED naming the new site. This is the criterion that stops the CLASS of bug, not just this bug.

Given an executor raising RuntimeError, when POST /trips/{id}/compose is called, then the response is NOT a 422 carrying reason 'compose_verification_failed', and the server log carries the exception type and message. A crash must never be blamed on the narrator's content.

Given a VERIFY refusal on the preview path, when the response is read, then the untraceable-sentence provenance (stop index, source_type, source_id, cited ids, counts) is on the wire rather than only in /tmp/ondoway-workbench-api.log, and the log-only loop is DELETED in the same change so no dead path remains.

Given a crash-state payload, when the workbench renders it, then it shows a distinct loud failure element naming the exception type and message -- NOT the calm blue .tour-basic-lane note; and given a policy-state payload it renders the existing calm blue note and no failure element. The existing honesty tests test_tour_preview_renders_basic_lane_honestly and test_standalone_tour_preview_renders_basic_lane_honestly stay byte-identical and green, which is what proves the tourist-facing page was not made scary.

Given real Render credentials and a real Paris start with 2+ routable stops, when a tour is generated through the running workbench in a real browser, then narration_kind is llm_candidate, compose_status is composed, every stop carries non-empty narration, no blue 'Basic grounded guide' banner appears, and the string 'cannot enter context' appears nowhere in the response or the API log. This is the founding case and the ONLY thing that proves the fix.
make lint produces zero errors. Baseline is green today, so any error is ours.

Given ONE identical tour request, when it is put through the workbench surface and the phone surface, then a parity harness captures both full outputs and reports every field that differs. This is the INSTRUMENT, and it must exist before any divergence is fixed, so every fix is proven by a before/after number on the real artifact rather than by reading.

Given one identical request put through both surfaces, when the two tour payloads are compared, then they are IDENTICAL -- every field, no exceptions, NO ALLOWLIST. OWNER RULING 2026-08-03 verbatim: 'ANY DIFFERENCE. NO EXCEPTIONS. STOP FLINCHING.' The two exceptions this planner originally reserved were withdrawn as not being output differences at all: route SOURCE is an input path (same planner, same request, same route), and review-only diagnostics must be COMPUTED on both surfaces and merely not DISPLAYED by the phone. The only permitted difference between the two surfaces is what each UI chooses to draw.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-03 verbatim: 'ALL OF THAT CODE HAS TO BE SHARED. NO DIVERGENCES.' Given the tree after Track B, when the syntax tree of src/ is walked, then every tour-building internal -- route planning, stop selection, beat selection, narration, the fact-check gates, duplicate removal and audio construction -- has EXACTLY ONE caller, and that caller is the single shared tour service. A second call site FAILS THE BUILD naming the offending site. This is the mechanism, not the parity comparison: comparing outputs DETECTS drift after someone writes it, whereas one implementation makes drift impossible to write. Detection assumes someone is watching; nobody is. The check must be SELF-COMPLETING, not list-based: it derives its subjects by reachability from the single shared entry point, so ANY tour logic not reachable through that door fails -- there is no hand-maintained list that can go stale, and a NEW stage added outside the door breaks the build the minute it is written. REQUIRED MUTATIONS: add a second call site to any tour-building internal, and separately add a NEW tour-logic module that nothing registers anywhere; both must go RED naming the offending site.

A PERIODIC MODEL-DRIVEN ARCHITECTURE AUDIT exists, run deliberately and NOT part of `make test`. It reads the tour code and answers one question the deterministic checks cannot: is any tour logic RE-IMPLEMENTED rather than shared -- same behaviour written twice, each copy with exactly one caller, so both the boundary test and the output comparison pass? Its output is a WORKLIST, never a verdict. HARD RULE, written into the audit itself: a model finding is NEVER a pass. Green from the model means nothing and may never be reported as proof of parity; red means go look, and the lead is not closed until it has been converted into a DETERMINISTIC check. Rationale for keeping it out of the bar: an LLM verdict is non-deterministic (a flaky gate destroys trust in the whole suite, and this project bans re-running for green), it costs money on every run, and above all it is EXACTLY the failure mode being fixed -- on 2026-08-03 I read this architecture and concluded 'unified' while 11 things differed. A model reading architecture is a review, and the lesson of that day is to stop reviewing and start measuring.

Given the single shared tour service, when its signature is inspected, then it accepts the tour REQUEST and nothing that can change what the tour IS -- no gate switch, no policy object, no cap, no segmentation mode. Every such setting lives INSIDE the shared module. This is the exact hole that produced the fact-check divergence: one shared function called with different arguments is two different algorithms. REQUIRED MUTATION: add a behaviour-changing parameter to the shared entry point and this goes RED.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-03, ordered FIRST AND FOREMOST: every leg of every served tour is a REAL walking route returned by the routing engine, carrying its receipt. The straight-line fallback (haversine distance x 1.35, src/tour/routing.py:191-199) is DELETED from the served path, not merely shared -- it can path a walker through buildings, across the Seine, or onto the wrong side of a railway. A tour whose legs cannot be routed is REFUSED, never silently degraded. Both surfaces behave identically because there is only one implementation.

Given a served tour's stop sequence handed to the routing engine as walking directions, when the resulting path is inspected, then a person could actually follow it: consecutive legs join end-to-start, metres of route inside the Seine outside a bridge corridor is ~0 (src/tour/audit.py::seine_crossing_metres), a round trip returns to its start, a point-to-point reaches its destination, no stop is revisited, and the honest ETA (real routed seconds plus standing time, src/tour/audit.py::route_eta_seconds) matches what the tour promised within the stated tolerance. Routing is LOCAL and therefore FREE, so this runs across many start points and durations rather than one.

Given the parity harness, when it runs, then it FIRST asserts it actually found and executed both surfaces and captured non-empty output from each. A harness that silently compares nothing to nothing must fail, never pass.

Given the syntax tree of every call site of the shared finalizer finalize_certification_composition, when the three gate arguments (faithfulness_checker, enforce_claim_coverage, scan_glue_for_invention) are compared, then every live-API call site passes the SAME values. Derived with ast, never text matching, and the test asserts it found the call sites before asserting anything about them. REQUIRED MUTATION: drop one gate argument from either surface and this goes RED naming the surface and the argument.

Given a tour generated through the workbench, when the narration is produced, then the real faithfulness checker, the claim-coverage baseline and the glue invention scan ALL ran -- provably, by injecting narration that each gate must reject and asserting the workbench refuses it exactly as the phone does. Today the workbench substitutes MockFaithfulnessChecker, which approves every sentence.

Given one identical request, when both surfaces plan a route, then they seat the SAME stops in the SAME order with the SAME time budget. Today the workbench plans 60 minutes and caps at 8 stops where the phone plans 50 and allows up to 15 -- these figures are DERIVED FROM CONSTANTS and must be MEASURED live by step P0 before being treated as fact.

Given one identical stop, when audio is produced for each surface, then the editor hears exactly the file the tourist hears: same segmentation, same text, same length cap. Today the phone voices walk + walk-past + standing narration as ONE file while the workbench voices three separate cards with vignette text stripped, and the workbench truncates at 6000 characters while the phone has no cap.

Given a stop with a deep-dive (keep-exploring) narration, when the workbench renders it, then the editor can read and hear that narration. Today the workbench receives only a boolean flag, so the owner cannot review that text at all.

Given the same injected fault, when it hits each surface, then both surfaces report it the same way and both run inside a degradation scope. Today degradation_scope exists only on the workbench route, so a clean workbench run does not prove a clean phone run.

Given the tree after Track B, when the superseded duplicate paths are searched for, then they are ABSENT -- no unified behaviour is added alongside a retained old path. The owner has named leaving old code as dead code a repeat offence.

Given a claim and its cited sources, when the scorer runs, then ONE judge call returns a SCORE, the exact SPAN it cannot support, and the claim TYPE (hard fact / inference / atmosphere). A low score carrying no span is DISCARDED as a bad verdict -- that is the only mechanism that catches a broken scorer. Atmosphere claims are never scored and can never block. MEASURED motivation: the binary gate flagged "Look hard at the facade, because it's a manifesto of Art Nouveau" (the source's own sentence, two words changed) with the SAME output it gave a genuine invention, so severity was unrecoverable from the report.

Given a tour, when it is judged, then NO AVERAGE is taken and no single sentence blocks. Scores are per CLAIM, not per sentence. REQUIRED NEGATIVE: a tour of 149 well-supported claims plus ONE fabricated claim must be caught -- an average would score 0.944 and ship it, and longer tours dilute further.

Given a claim scoring low, when the engine responds, then it RE-AUTHORS that one stop with the unsupported span named and rescores; the claim is cut only if still low after ONE repair. Bounded loop; the default outcome is a better tour, never a shorter one.

Given a low-scoring claim, when it is triaged, then the score is compared against what its SOURCE could support at best: score low + source rich = the writer invented (repair the tour); score low + source thin = the beat is too poor (repair the corpus). An absolute threshold blames the writer for corpus poverty, which is where most of this project's lost time has gone.

Given the same (beat_id, claim, wording), when it has been scored once, then it is not rescored -- and a beat whose claims score low across MANY DIFFERENT tours is emitted to the corpus repair queue. The cache IS the backlog; no separate pipeline is built.

Given a change to the scorer's prompt or model, when the labelled set (~50 owner-ruled sentences, half sound, half genuinely invented) is rescored, then agreement below the pinned rate REJECTS the change. Reuses the existing pinned-prompt-fingerprint pattern. Without it the scorer drifts silently.

Given the scorer, when it is calibrated, then the threshold is DERIVED from the owner's gold text and the human reference tours (must pass) against a deliberately corrupted tour with injected inventions (must fail). If gold and corrupted do NOT separate, the scorer is broken and no threshold rescues it. The agent does not pick the number.

Given the scored path, when it ships, then verify_claim_coverage (src/tour/claim_dedup.py:388, lexical) is DELETED -- the reverse-direction score replaces it. It produced the false 'Square named for Henri IV was dropped' report on a tour that plainly says it. No old path is left beside the new one.

Given any tour, when the gate decides, then EXACTLY ONE condition blocks: a hard-fact claim still scoring low AFTER a repair attempt, against a source rich enough to have supported it. Everything else RECORDS. A check may block only when it can NAME the specific thing that is wrong; a check that can only say 'I don't know' records.

Given the corpus fact-check, when a claim is checked against the held-out authority set, then there are THREE verdicts: confirmed / contradicted / NOT COVERED, and 'not covered' RECORDS AND SHIPS. If 'not covered' blocked there would be no tours at all, since no heritage register holds an opinion on when a draper opened a shop.

Given the two source sets, when they are assembled, then no source used in the CORPUS appears in the AUTHORITY set, enforced mechanically and split by ORIGINAL PROVENANCE rather than by file. Leakage is the ML analogy's own failure mode: Wikipedia and most guidebooks descend from the same older works, so agreement proves nothing if the authority derives from the corpus.

steps.name: The swallowed premium failure puts its real cause on the wire and records a degradation
A VERIFY refusal names what failed on the wire; delete the log-only loop
A compose crash is never relabelled a verification failure (the phone path)

run.note: THREE LIVE ACCEPTANCE RUNS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ENGINE STEPS. The ledger contract pins test_command to a single pytest node id, and a real-provider tour in a real browser cannot be one. They are performed by the main agent WITH THE OWNER WATCHING, and no green node-id test may stand in for them: (1) MEASURE-FIRST -- one identical request through both surfaces before any convergence work, because the 60-vs-50-minute and 8-vs-15-stop figures are derived from constants, not measured; (2) THE FOUNDING CASE -- a real Paris premium tour composing end to end through make workbench, which is the only proof the crash is fixed (AC-14); (3) THE FINAL PARITY PROOF -- one request, both surfaces, outputs identical with no allowlist. The engine still exercises the browser shard through its own phase gates.
